title: Cap. X Arg. IV: if God passed over none except from foresight of sufficient grace finally despised, it would lie in each one's power to be reprobated or not — elect/reprobate difference would first arise from human wills, not diverse divine placita
pass_a_gloss: If God passed over or reprobated no one except from foresight of his sufficient grace finally despised and contemned, or (which comes to the same) from foresight of final impenitence and unbelief, then it would be situated in the power of every one, that according to his own choice he be reprobated or not reprobated, and be elect or non-elect. Nay, every discrimination of the elect and reprobate would first arise not from diverse placita of the Divine will, but from diverse acts of human wills.
pass_b_english: Suppose God passed over or reprobated no one except from foresight of his sufficient grace finally despised and contemned — or, what comes to the same thing, from foresight of final impenitence and unbelief. Then it would lie in each person's power, at his own choice, whether he be reprobated or not, elect or non-elect. Nay more: the whole difference between elect and reprobate would first spring not from diverse placita of the divine will, but from diverse acts of human wills.
source_text: Si Deus neminem praeteriret aut reprobaret nisi ex praevisione gratiae suae sufficientis finaliter spretæ et contemptae, sive (quod eodem redit) ex praevisione finalis impoenitentiae et infidelitatis, tum situm esset in potestate uniuscujusque, ut pro arbitrio suo reprobetur vel non reprobetur, atque electus vel non-electus esset. Imo omne discrimen electorum et reprobatorum non ex diversis placitis Divinae voluntatis, sed ex diversis actibus humanarum voluntatum primo exoriretur.
